episode.title: The Things We Leave Behind
intro: A few days before Emma and Ren leave for a three-month assignment, Claire plans a farewell dinner at Kamo House. Leo cooks, Nao brings a handmade cup, and Claire makes a photo album. Emma and Leo talk calmly outside. They cannot change the past, but they can learn from it and wish each other well.
エマとレンが3か月の現地勤務に出発する数日前、クレアがKamo Houseで送別の夕食を計画します。レオは料理を作り、ナオは手作りのカップを持ってきて、クレアは写真アルバムを作ります。エマとレオは外で落ち着いて話します。過去は変えられませんが、学び、互いの幸せを願えます。
goal: I can read farewell notes and reply with thanks and a clear plan.
送別のメモを読み、感謝と具体的な予定で返事ができる。
episode.warmup: What makes a farewell message specific, not only polite?
words: I am grateful for your support during the project.
Please confirm you can join the first group call.
The bakery is still being fitted out, so it is not open yet.
The opening date is not yet confirmed.
Use the group chat for small updates between calls.
This is a temporary assignment, not a permanent goodbye.
discussion: You are Emma. Your tutor is Claire. Thank her for one clear memory and suggest how you will keep in touch.
あなたはエマ役、講師はクレア役です。具体的な思い出を一つ挙げて感謝し、連絡方法を提案しましょう。
episode.followup: How can you turn “keep in touch” into a realistic plan?

rule: Use “Looking back, …” and “I have learned …” with one specific memory.
「Looking back, …」「I have learned …」を使い、具体的な思い出を一つ入れましょう。
examples: Looking back, your invitation on my first day helped me a lot.
振り返ると、初日に誘ってくれたことがとても助けになりました。

rule: Use “Please confirm …” and give a clear time, place, and person.
「Please confirm …」を使い、時間・場所・誰が送るかをはっきり書きましょう。
examples: Please confirm you can join at 8 p.m. in Kyoto. Ren will send the link.
京都の午後8時に参加できるか確認してください。リンクはレンが送ります。

situation: Read three notes for a farewell album. Find each person’s memory, lesson, or hope.
送別アルバムの3つのメモを読みましょう。思い出、学び、希望を探しましょう。
apply.text:
Notes for the farewell album
Claire: I remember inviting Emma downstairs on her first day. Now she helps build projects that bring people together. Looking back, I have learned that welcoming one person can start a bigger story.

Nao: Emma noticed my camera before she knew much about my ceramics. Our walks gave me a friend and photos. I am grateful for her encouragement before my gallery presentation. I hope we keep sharing small updates, not only big achievements.

Emma: I was not honest when things became difficult. I regret that. I cannot undo that, but I have learned to communicate more clearly. Three months away is not the end of these friendships.
questions: Who remembers the first invitation downstairs?
What updates does Nao hope to share?
Small updates as well as big achievements.
Is the assignment a permanent goodbye?

situation: You are Emma at the farewell dinner. Your tutor is Claire. Read the new dinner note, then respond with thanks and a clear plan.
あなたは送別の夕食にいるエマ役、講師はクレア役です。新しいメモを読んで、感謝と具体的な予定で返事をしましょう。
task: Thank two friends for specific things. Say one thing you learned. Confirm the first call plan. Say that the bakery is not open yet.
二人に具体的に感謝し、学んだことを一つ言いましょう。最初の通話予定を確認し、パン屋はまだ開いていないと伝えましょう。
mission.text:
Tonight and the next three months
Farewell dinner - Claire’s new note
Leo has prepared dinner. Riverbend Bakery is still being fitted out, so its opening date is not yet confirmed. He will send photos when it is ready.

Nao has made Emma a travel cup and is preparing pieces for her upcoming Fukuoka exhibition. Claire has finished the photo album.

Emma and Ren have accepted the three-month Seoul assignment. They will return to their Japan-based roles afterward.

First group video call: the first Sunday after arrival, at 8 p.m. in Kyoto. Ren will send the invitation link. Please confirm you can join. Use the group chat for small updates between calls. Later call dates will be agreed separately.
mission.title: Tonight and the next three months
lines: Emma, who do you want to thank tonight, and why?
Can you thank two people with specific details?
What is one thing you have learned at Kamo House?
Is Riverbend Bakery open now, or not open yet?

mission.evidence: Tutor evidence note: Student should use details from the note: bakery not open yet, opening date not confirmed, Leo cooked dinner, Nao made a travel cup and has an upcoming Fukuoka exhibition, Claire finished the album, three-month Seoul assignment then return to Japan-based roles, first call is first Sunday after arrival at 8 p.m. Kyoto time, Ren sends the link, group chat for small updates, later call dates not fixed. Do not say the bakery is already open or the exhibition is already finished.

topics: What makes a thank-you message specific?
What small gift can hold a strong memory?
What is one thing you can write in an album?
What makes a call plan realistic?
What small update can you share this week?
How can you suggest a different time politely?
How can you say sorry without many excuses?
What can you do differently next time?
How can friends move forward without changing the past?
trivia: “Keep in touch” is friendly, but it does not set a time. A plan like “the first Sunday at 8 p.m.” is a real arrangement.
「Keep in touch」は親しみの表現ですが、時間は決めていません。「最初の日曜日の午後8時」などは具体的な約束です。
triviaQuestion: Which words fix a call time, not only a friendly wish?
The first Sunday after arrival at 8 p.m. in Kyoto.
episode.closing: At the farewell dinner, they share food, a handmade cup, and a photo album. Emma and Leo accept the past and wish each other well. Emma and Ren leave for the three-month assignment with a first group call planned. Leo’s bakery opening and Nao’s exhibition are still ahead.
